title: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookwood, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookwood, AL | Black Warrior CBM Core
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane minerals near Brookwood, AL? Get a hedged, activity-based cash offer tied directly to Brookwood and Oak Grove field production data.
heroLead: Brookwood sits at the center of the Black Warrior Basin's most productive coalbed methane ground, home to the Brookwood and Oak Grove fields that made this corner of Tuscaloosa County one of the most closely watched coal-gas plays in the country during its peak.
intro: The Brookwood field, developed alongside the deep longwall coal mining operations that ran beneath much of the area, became one of the defining examples of coalbed methane production in the United States starting in the 1980s, drawing gas from the same Pottsville coal seams that also fed the underground mines. Mineral owners here are more likely than almost anywhere else in Alabama to have an actual royalty history to point to, and a well close enough to matter.

sections.heading: Why Brookwood became the Black Warrior Basin's core
paragraphs: Dense well spacing and coordinated development around the underground coal mining operations here made Brookwood and the neighboring Oak Grove field the heart of Alabama's coalbed methane industry through the 1990s and 2000s. Production has declined significantly from those peak years as the shallower, easiest-to-produce gas depleted, but well control in this area remains denser than almost anywhere else in the state.

sections.heading: What a producing interest looks like here
paragraphs: If your family holds a Brookwood-area interest with an actual royalty statement history, we look closely at that well's production trend, since CBM wells characteristically decline faster in their early years before leveling into a longer, lower-rate tail. A well several years into its life is valued differently than one still in its early decline curve.

sections.heading: Interests without current production
paragraphs: Even within the Brookwood core, some tracts sit between existing wells or outside the current spacing unit and have no production history of their own. Those are still valued against the surrounding field's activity, though the range reflects the absence of a direct royalty stream.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership through Tuscaloosa County records
paragraphs: Given how much leasing activity has moved through the Brookwood area over four decades, tracing a specific fractional interest through Tuscaloosa County's deed and probate records is often a real research project. We do that work as part of every offer, since an accurate ownership percentage matters more here than almost anywhere else in the basin.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Brookwood interest is inside an active spacing unit?
faqs.answer: We check Alabama Oil and Gas Board field orders and current permit records against your specific parcel to determine whether it sits inside an established unit and what well control exists nearby.

faqs.question: My family has received royalty checks for years, but the amount keeps dropping. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Coalbed methane wells in the Brookwood-Oak Grove trend typically show a fast initial decline followed by a long, lower-rate production tail, so shrinking checks over time are the expected pattern rather than a red flag.

faqs.question: Does the underground coal mining in this area affect the gas rights separately?
faqs.answer: Coal and coalbed methane gas can be held by different owners depending on how the original severance was recorded, so we review the deed language carefully to confirm exactly what mineral interest you hold before quoting.

faqs.question: Why would a Brookwood-area interest be worth more than one elsewhere in Jefferson or Walker County?
faqs.answer: Well density and production history here are generally higher than in the basin's flank areas, which typically supports a stronger range, though every tract is still priced against its own specific well control and current activity.
